html:
SMTO-EXE-0215 — SMTO couldn't turn the PDF page into an image

GUID: e12fae7d-0523-5a13-b9dc-0a3e7925a50f
Slug: pdf-render-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • SMTO tried to make a picture of a PDF page, and the drawing step failed. No image was saved, and your original PDF was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO for an image of a different page of the same PDF. This message does not establish what went wrong, but if other pages work, the problem is limited to that one page.
  2. Ask for the failing page again at a standard quality, such as 144 DPI, rather than a high setting. This rules out the quality setting as the cause.
  3. Open the page in your usual PDF viewer to see whether it displays correctly. A page that also fails elsewhere points to a damaged page rather than an SMTO problem.

What success looks like

  • An image of the page appears under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the page number and whether it opens in your viewer, to the person who manages SMTO. Keep the original PDF unchanged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDFium renderer on the Gateway raised an unclassified error while rendering the requested page (not a memory, recursion, size or permission limit).

What this means

  • Native PDF rendering raised an exception outside the explicit memory/recursion bound and permission checks. The generic failure does not establish a malformed page or missing backend. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Native PDF rendering raised an exception outside the explicit memory/recursion bound and permission checks. The generic failure does not establish a malformed page or missing backend.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect page selection, DPI, document permissions and bounded renderer diagnostics; preserve specific known prerequisite failures separately.

How to fix it

  • Document.render maps unclassified pypdfium2 exceptions to render_failed; the cause is not established. Retry a single page at the default 144 DPI to isolate a failing page, check whether flattening AcroForm fields for rendering is involved, verify the pypdfium2 version is supported (5.x), and report a reproducible page with the error details.
  • Inspect the failed page, settings and renderer evidence; correct the established cause before a new render request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported page renders at valid DPI into a bounded verified image.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
